motion: We should make school lunches free for all students.
note: A帯前後想定のLOスピーチ。Government Point 1への反論・Opposition Point 1/2・Point 1の説明を含むが、S帯の固有性・比較はやや弱い。
pmSpeech: Ladies and gentlemen, today's motion is that we should make school lunches free for all students. We have two points. Our first point is that free school lunches protect children's health. Some families cannot afford good food, and children from these families sometimes skip lunch or eat only bread. If lunch is free for everyone, every child eats a warm and balanced meal every day. For example, imagine a boy whose parents both work but still cannot pay the monthly lunch fee; he feels ashamed and eats alone. Free lunch removes this shame and this hunger. Our second point is that free lunches reduce the burden on parents and support families raising children. Let me explain our first point in more detail. Health in childhood decides health for the whole life. A child who does not eat enough cannot concentrate in the afternoon classes, gets sick more often, and falls behind. Only the government can guarantee that no child is hungry at school, because charity and individual effort always miss someone. That is why we proudly propose this motion.
transcript: Hello everyone. As the Leader of the Opposition, we strongly oppose today's motion, that we should make school lunches free for all students. First, let me respond to the government's first point about health. The Prime Minister said that free lunch protects children's health because poor families cannot pay. But this argument has a problem. There is already a system that supports poor families: in Japan, families with low income can get lunch fees paid by the city. So the children the government talked about are already protected. Making lunch free for all students means paying also for rich families who can easily pay by themselves. That does not protect anyone's health more. Now let me present our two points. Our first point is that free lunch for everyone wastes limited education budget. Our second point is that the quality of lunches will go down. Let me explain our first point in detail. The money for schools is limited. If the city pays lunch for all students, including rich families, it must cut money from somewhere else, such as new textbooks, air conditioners, or support staff for students who need help. For example, one city near us delayed repairing the old gym because the budget went to free lunch for everyone. Helping only the families who really need it costs much less, and the rest of the money can improve education for all children. This is why targeted support is better than free lunch for everyone. About our second point, if the budget becomes tight, schools may buy cheaper ingredients, so the quality of lunch becomes lower for every student. For these reasons, we oppose this motion. Thank you.
